label: title
text:
Sixteen lost pets became something else inside that house.
Eight kids are going in to bring the rest home.

NEW EXPEDITION
Choose a Kid, a Companion, and go in
PLAY TOGETHER
Meet at the treehouse and go in with somebody else
THE MENAGERIE
The clubhouse, the board, the roster
SETTINGS
Sound, motion, readability
CREDITS

label: opening-1
text:
THE FIRST NIGHT

Maya Chen
13

Practical, organised, observant, stubborn, dryly funny. Uses forearm crutches.

Checked the Batteries

Backpack Gear has one extra use per expedition, and Gear never breaks in the first region.

Backpack preparation and equipment specialisation

Orbit
BLACK DOMESTIC CAT, WHITE PATCH ON HIS CHEST

Orbit’s collar was outside the mansion. Orbit wasn’t.

SKIP — I KNOW THE HOUSE

label: opening-ready
text:
THE FIRST NIGHT

Amina Okafor
11

Gentle, patient, the one who notices when someone needs to stop.

Blanket Fort Builder

Safe Rooms restore an extra chunk of Courage and let you keep one Snack.

Courage recovery, long expeditions, animal Curiosities

Mochi
LOP-EARED RABBIT

Mochi disappeared from the pen. The latch was shut. There was strange moss under the shelter.

label: maya-opening
text:
THE FIRST NIGHT

Maya Chen
looking for Orbit

“Orbit’s collar was outside the mansion. Orbit wasn’t.”

“He scratches three times when he wants a door opened. I’m listening.”

“I packed a flashlight, spare batteries, and snacks. The snacks are not spare.”

GO ON
SKIP — I KNOW THE HOUSE

label: opening-2
text:
THE FIRST NIGHT

Eight kids spread their clues across the pavement. Different pets. Different disappearances. The same old mansion.

They pack flashlights, snacks and a first-aid kit.

Someone adds another snack. A sensible precaution.

GO ON
SKIP — I KNOW THE HOUSE

label: opening-3
text:
THE FIRST NIGHT

Inside: dust, dark corners, one very clean welcome mat.

The door clicks shut. Where the way back should be, a different hallway waits.

The welcome mat says PLEASE WIPE YOUR FEET.

It has priorities.

GO ON
SKIP — I KNOW THE HOUSE

label: opening-4
text:
THE FIRST NIGHT

Marmalade
the Ghost Cat

A cat sits in the hallway. You can see the wallpaper through her.

She washes one paw. Her collar tag reads MARMALADE.

Something under the furniture sneezes. Marmalade stops washing.

Apparently, that was rude.

GO ON
SKIP — I KNOW THE HOUSE

label: opening-5
text:
THE FIRST NIGHT

Marmalade
the Ghost Cat

A Dust Bunny bounces out from under a chair.

The ghost cat steps beside you. Her tail points toward the trouble.

You have a partner.

Look closer
Who gets an answer?

Are the bells broken, or is one kind of call being blocked?

My idea — optional. You can change it.
The bells need fixing.
One kind of call is being blocked.
I’m not sure yet.
Try the worn WATER cord.

You pull the worn cord. Its bell rings clearly.

A jug fills a clean dish at the counter. It waits until the water stops wobbling before sliding it over.

Try the third bell’s test lever.

The third plate reads HELP GOING HOME. You press its lever. The bell rings perfectly.

A padded cover drops around that bell and muffles it. When you release the lever, the cover folds back.

What happened

Both bells work. The water call brought care. The going-home call was covered before anyone answered.

The unreachable cord belongs to that same covered bell.

Marmalade

the Ghost Cat

The agile technical Companion. Poor conventional defence and only moderate raw damage — what makes her powerful is avoiding attacks entirely, punishing enemies for trying to hit her, spending Nine Lives for bursts, and chaining lots of small actions together. High skill ceiling: she rewards reading intents and planning a turn ahead.

SIGNATURE MECHANICS
Ghoststep
Each stack cancels the next hit of enemy Attack damage. Not Guard — one stack eats a 20-damage swing, but a six-hit flurry chews straight through it.
Haunt
Haunted enemies hurt themselves whenever they attack. It dissipates as it triggers.
Nine Lives
She starts every Scuffle with 9 Lives. Powerful Tricks spend them. They do not come back until the next fight.
Zoomies
Effects that only fire on the third or later Trick you play this turn.
Untouched
Bonuses if she lost no Courage during the last enemy turn.
STRENGTHS
High card mobility
Cancels single huge attacks outright
Powerful reactive damage
Strong draw
Excellent 0-cost chains
Converts defence into offence
WEAKNESSES
Unreliable conventional Guard
Multi-hit attacks strip Ghoststep fast
Little straightforward heavy damage
Nine Lives are finite per fight
Haunt is dead against passive enemies

Ghoststep & Untouched

label: attic-arrival

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below three dog portraits. The third frame is empty.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

NR-lampworks-clue-1.title: A familiar shadow
lines: Long rabbit ears rise on the wall behind a lantern. One ear quivers.

NR-lampworks-clue-2.title: The covered hooks
lines: Two rows of hooks are marked OUT and BACK. A board covers OUT.

NR-lampworks-clue-3.title: The moth’s appointment
lines: A Lamp Moth circles a lamp marked CIRCLING BY APPOINTMENT.

CASE-foyer-bells-water: You pull the worn cord. Its bell rings clearly.
A jug fills a clean dish at the counter. It waits until the water stops wobbling before sliding it over.
CASE-foyer-bells-home: The third plate reads HELP GOING HOME. You press its lever. The bell rings perfectly.
A padded cover drops around that bell and muffles it. When you release the lever, the cover folds back.

CASE-lampworks-shadow-turn: As you turn the shade, the long ears become two round handles. The metal loops turn with them.
You turn it back. The rabbit-shaped ears return in exactly the same place.
CASE-lampworks-shadow-panel: Through the clear panel, you can see the lantern’s floor and all four sides. Only a wick and flame are inside.
Two tall metal loops curl around the outside of the shade.

AFTER-foyer.label: Point out the waiting hatch.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You pointed out the waiting hatch. The Butler caught the dish and served the animal its water.

Around The Moonlit Attic and Observatory

A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.

Look closer
A window in two futures

Does the warning show what must happen?

My idea — optional. You can change it.
The warning must come true.
It shows something that might happen.
I’m not sure yet.
Read both cards.

The front card says NEXT TOUCH: BALL BREAKS WINDOW. Behind it: NEXT TOUCH: BALL SQUASHES. WINDOW HOLDS.

Both show this ball and this pane of glass. Neither card has been crossed out.

Gently press the soft ball against the glass.

You press the soft ball against the window. It squashes flat, then springs back as you lift it away.

The glass stays whole. You return the ball to the sill.

What happened

Two cards showed the same next touch ending differently. The gentle test matched the card hidden at the back.

The frightening card was not the only possibility.

label: entered-room

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below three dog portraits. The third frame is empty.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

NR-lampworks-clue-1.title: A familiar shadow
lines: Long rabbit ears rise on the wall behind a lantern. One ear quivers.

NR-lampworks-clue-2.title: The covered hooks
lines: Two rows of hooks are marked OUT and BACK. A board covers OUT.

NR-lampworks-clue-3.title: The moth’s appointment
lines: A Lamp Moth circles a lamp marked CIRCLING BY APPOINTMENT.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.

CASE-foyer-bells-water: You pull the worn cord. Its bell rings clearly.
A jug fills a clean dish at the counter. It waits until the water stops wobbling before sliding it over.
CASE-foyer-bells-home: The third plate reads HELP GOING HOME. You press its lever. The bell rings perfectly.
A padded cover drops around that bell and muffles it. When you release the lever, the cover folds back.

CASE-lampworks-shadow-turn: As you turn the shade, the long ears become two round handles. The metal loops turn with them.
You turn it back. The rabbit-shaped ears return in exactly the same place.
CASE-lampworks-shadow-panel: Through the clear panel, you can see the lantern’s floor and all four sides. Only a wick and flame are inside.
Two tall metal loops curl around the outside of the shade.

CASE-attic-window-ball: You press the soft ball against the window. It squashes flat, then springs back as you lift it away.
The glass stays whole. You return the ball to the sill.
CASE-attic-window-cards: The front card says NEXT TOUCH: BALL BREAKS WINDOW. Behind it: NEXT TOUCH: BALL SQUASHES. WINDOW HOLDS.
Both show this ball and this pane of glass. Neither card has been crossed out.

AFTER-foyer.label: Point out the waiting hatch.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You pointed out the waiting hatch. The Butler caught the dish and served the animal its water.

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below three dog portraits. The third frame is empty.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

NR-lampworks-clue-1.title: A familiar shadow
lines: Long rabbit ears rise on the wall behind a lantern. One ear quivers.

NR-lampworks-clue-2.title: The covered hooks
lines: Two rows of hooks are marked OUT and BACK. A board covers OUT.

NR-lampworks-clue-3.title: The moth’s appointment
lines: A Lamp Moth circles a lamp marked CIRCLING BY APPOINTMENT.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

CASE-foyer-bells-water: You pull the worn cord. Its bell rings clearly.
A jug fills a clean dish at the counter. It waits until the water stops wobbling before sliding it over.
CASE-foyer-bells-home: The third plate reads HELP GOING HOME. You press its lever. The bell rings perfectly.
A padded cover drops around that bell and muffles it. When you release the lever, the cover folds back.

CASE-lampworks-shadow-turn: As you turn the shade, the long ears become two round handles. The metal loops turn with them.
You turn it back. The rabbit-shaped ears return in exactly the same place.
CASE-lampworks-shadow-panel: Through the clear panel, you can see the lantern’s floor and all four sides. Only a wick and flame are inside.
Two tall metal loops curl around the outside of the shade.

CASE-attic-window-ball: You press the soft ball against the window. It squashes flat, then springs back as you lift it away.
The glass stays whole. You return the ball to the sill.
CASE-attic-window-cards: The front card says NEXT TOUCH: BALL BREAKS WINDOW. Behind it: NEXT TOUCH: BALL SQUASHES. WINDOW HOLDS.
Both show this ball and this pane of glass. Neither card has been crossed out.

AFTER-foyer.label: Point out the waiting hatch.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You pointed out the waiting hatch. The Butler caught the dish and served the animal its water.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Give the Watcher room to act.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You left room. The Watcher caught the telescope and cleared the other warnings from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Ask, “Who ordered the soup?”
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You asked who ordered the soup. A mouse chef directed the Confectioner to put away the icing and use the spoon plain.

NR-lampworks-clue-1.title: A familiar shadow
lines: Long rabbit ears rise on the wall behind a lantern. One ear quivers.

NR-lampworks-clue-2.title: The covered hooks

NR-lampworks-clue-3.title: The moth’s appointment

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below three dog portraits. The third frame is empty.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

NR-lampworks-clue-1.title: A familiar shadow
lines: Long rabbit ears rise on the wall behind a lantern. One ear quivers.

NR-lampworks-clue-2.title: The covered hooks
lines: Two rows of hooks are marked OUT and BACK. A board covers OUT.

NR-lampworks-clue-3.title: The moth’s appointment
lines: A Lamp Moth circles a lamp marked CIRCLING BY APPOINTMENT.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

CASE-foyer-bells-water: You pull the worn cord. Its bell rings clearly.
A jug fills a clean dish at the counter. It waits until the water stops wobbling before sliding it over.
CASE-foyer-bells-home: The third plate reads HELP GOING HOME. You press its lever. The bell rings perfectly.
A padded cover drops around that bell and muffles it. When you release the lever, the cover folds back.

CASE-lampworks-shadow-turn: As you turn the shade, the long ears become two round handles. The metal loops turn with them.
You turn it back. The rabbit-shaped ears return in exactly the same place.
CASE-lampworks-shadow-panel: Through the clear panel, you can see the lantern’s floor and all four sides. Only a wick and flame are inside.
Two tall metal loops curl around the outside of the shade.

CASE-attic-window-ball: You press the soft ball against the window. It squashes flat, then springs back as you lift it away.
The glass stays whole. You return the ball to the sill.
CASE-attic-window-cards: The front card says NEXT TOUCH: BALL BREAKS WINDOW. Behind it: NEXT TOUCH: BALL SQUASHES. WINDOW HOLDS.
Both show this ball and this pane of glass. Neither card has been crossed out.

AFTER-foyer.label: Point out the waiting hatch.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You pointed out the waiting hatch. The Butler caught the dish and served the animal its water.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Give the Watcher room to act.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You left room. The Watcher caught the telescope and cleared the other warnings from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Ask, “Who ordered the soup?”
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You asked who ordered the soup. A mouse chef directed the Confectioner to put away the icing and use the spoon plain.

lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below three dog portraits. The third frame is empty.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

NR-lampworks-clue-1.title: A familiar shadow
lines: Long rabbit ears rise on the wall behind a lantern. One ear quivers.

NR-lampworks-clue-2.title: The covered hooks
lines: Two rows of hooks are marked OUT and BACK. A board covers OUT.

NR-lampworks-clue-3.title: The moth’s appointment
lines: A Lamp Moth circles a lamp marked CIRCLING BY APPOINTMENT.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

CASE-foyer-bells-water: You pull the worn cord. Its bell rings clearly.
A jug fills a clean dish at the counter. It waits until the water stops wobbling before sliding it over.
CASE-foyer-bells-home: The third plate reads HELP GOING HOME. You press its lever. The bell rings perfectly.
A padded cover drops around that bell and muffles it. When you release the lever, the cover folds back.

CASE-lampworks-shadow-turn: As you turn the shade, the long ears become two round handles. The metal loops turn with them.
You turn it back. The rabbit-shaped ears return in exactly the same place.
CASE-lampworks-shadow-panel: Through the clear panel, you can see the lantern’s floor and all four sides. Only a wick and flame are inside.
Two tall metal loops curl around the outside of the shade.

CASE-attic-window-ball: You press the soft ball against the window. It squashes flat, then springs back as you lift it away.
The glass stays whole. You return the ball to the sill.
CASE-attic-window-cards: The front card says NEXT TOUCH: BALL BREAKS WINDOW. Behind it: NEXT TOUCH: BALL SQUASHES. WINDOW HOLDS.
Both show this ball and this pane of glass. Neither card has been crossed out.

AFTER-foyer.label: Point out the waiting hatch.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You pointed out the waiting hatch. The Butler caught the dish and served the animal its water.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Give the Watcher room to act.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You left room. The Watcher caught the telescope and cleared the other warnings from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Ask, “Who ordered the soup?”
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You asked who ordered the soup. A mouse chef directed the Confectioner to put away the icing and use the spoon plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Move a fallen leaf off the little path.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You cleared a small part of the path. The Conservatory opened the rest, and the seedling reached its chosen light.

Marmalade

the Ghost Cat

The agile technical Companion. Poor conventional defence and only moderate raw damage — what makes her powerful is avoiding attacks entirely, punishing enemies for trying to hit her, spending Nine Lives for bursts, and chaining lots of small actions together. High skill ceiling: she rewards reading intents and planning a turn ahead.

SIGNATURE MECHANICS
Ghoststep
Each stack cancels the next hit of enemy Attack damage. Not Guard — one stack eats a 20-damage swing, but a six-hit flurry chews straight through it.
Haunt
Haunted enemies hurt themselves whenever they attack. It dissipates as it triggers.
Nine Lives
She starts every Scuffle with 9 Lives. Powerful Tricks spend them. They do not come back until the next fight.
Zoomies
Effects that only fire on the third or later Trick you play this turn.
Untouched
Bonuses if she lost no Courage during the last enemy turn.
STRENGTHS
High card mobility
Cancels single huge attacks outright
Powerful reactive damage
Strong draw
Excellent 0-cost chains
Converts defence into offence
WEAKNESSES
Unreliable conventional Guard
Multi-hit attacks strip Ghoststep fast
Little straightforward heavy damage
Nine Lives are finite per fight
Haunt is dead against passive enemies

lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.

lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.

lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.

lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.

lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

label: entered-room

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.
detail: Two different pens made the marks. Neither tick has been erased.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

The Kennelmaster. Boss. Next: Check the Gates. Gains 6 Guard.. House Rule — LEASHED 0 / 3: It gains 3 Guard per stack at the end of your turn. lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.
detail: Two different pens made the marks. Neither tick has been erased.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.

detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.

detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.
detail: Two different pens made the marks. Neither tick has been erased.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.

lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed

detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.

detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

AFTER-heart.label: Tell the Keeper, “We can wait here.”
AFTER-heart.recap: You offered to wait. The Keeper opened the passage and left everyone room to decide what comes next.

END-GATE.label: Leave room for the animals.
END-GATE.recap: You left room. One animal stayed; another left and opened the gate from outside to return. The Keeper will wait for visitors.

lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

AFTER-heart.label: Tell the Keeper, “We can wait here.”
AFTER-heart.recap: You offered to wait. The Keeper opened the passage and left everyone room to decide what comes next.

END-GATE.label: Leave room for the animals.
END-GATE.recap: You left room. One animal stayed; another left and opened the gate from outside to return. The Keeper will wait for visitors.

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.
detail: Two different pens made the marks. Neither tick has been erased.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

AFTER-heart.label: Tell the Keeper, “We can wait here.”
AFTER-heart.recap: You offered to wait. The Keeper opened the passage and left everyone room to decide what comes next.

END-GATE.label: Leave room for the animals.
END-GATE.recap: You left room. One animal stayed; another left and opened the gate from outside to return. The Keeper will wait for visitors.

Orbit — homePepper — homeMochi — homeSprocket — homePixel — homeScout — homeMooncake — homeBean — home

Marmalade sleeps across the open doorway. Everyone carefully steps around her. The door remains open.

Drizzle makes one soft raindrop land in a cup. Then another. The rhythm is almost a song.

Drizzle watches a real cloud pass. For a moment the two clouds share one shadow.

Wink weaves a tiny hammock. You lean closer. Wink adds a curtain.

Wink hangs the hammock beside the entrance, with the curtain cord on the inside.

Taffy stretches toward a spoon. The spoon sticks. A second spoon is sent to help.

Taffy leaves a little gap around a new visitor instead of wrapping them in a hug. The visitor steps closer.

Brambleboo turns a leaf toward the torch. You move the torch closer. The leaf turns away. Back a little, then.

Brambleboo chooses a sunny patch outside, keeping one long root curled by the open door.

Mossbit studies a crumb. Then eats it. This took exactly as long as Mossbit required.

Mossbit rests halfway down the garden path. There is plenty of path left for everyone else.

Wisp tries to light the inside of a closed lunchbox. A thin blue line leaks out around the sandwich.

Wisp drifts outside, becomes one small light among many, then returns to light the step.

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.
detail: Two different pens made the marks. Neither tick has been erased.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

AFTER-heart.label: Tell the Keeper, “We can wait here.”
AFTER-heart.recap: You offered to wait. The Keeper opened the passage and left everyone room to decide what comes next.

END-GATE.label: Leave room for the animals.
END-GATE.recap: You left room. One animal stayed; another left and opened the gate from outside to return. The Keeper will wait for visitors.

NR-foyer-clue-1.title: Two answers
lines: An intake card has two ticks: FOUND ALONE and HAS A HOME.
detail: Two different pens made the marks. Neither tick has been erased.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

AFTER-heart.label: Tell the Keeper, “We can wait here.”
AFTER-heart.recap: You offered to wait. The Keeper opened the passage and left everyone room to decide what comes next.

END-GATE.label: Leave room for the animals.
END-GATE.recap: You left room. One animal stayed; another left and opened the gate from outside to return. The Keeper will wait for visitors.

detail: Two different pens made the marks. Neither tick has been erased.

NR-foyer-clue-2.title: The third cord
lines: Two bell cords are worn soft. A third ends in a neat knot high above the floor.
detail: The cords run in different directions. Each bell has a small test lever beside the counter.

NR-foyer-clue-3.title: A very patient brush
lines: A brush waits below two dog portraits and an empty frame.
detail: The first two read BEFORE BRUSHING and AFTER BRUSHING. The empty frame reads PLEASE REMAIN STILL.

PET-maya-trace.title: A small trace — Orbit
lines: Three scratches. A pause. Three more.
The marks stop beside a little door with a cat-sized handle.
detail: A black hair catches on the handle. Below it: a white one.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-1.title: The hidden strands
lines: A web surrounds a pawprint with three words. GETS LOST is tightly wrapped over the other two.
detail: Beneath the warning: GOES HOME and COMES BACK.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-2.title: The window warning
lines: A warning card hangs beside a window. A soft ball rests below the sill.
detail: A second card is pinned behind the first. Both show the same window.

NR-attic-observatory-clue-3.title: A tiny telescope
lines: A tiny telescope points through the wrong end of a much larger telescope.
detail: It can see one enormous biscuit beside the tea. The stars are elsewhere.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-1.title: Two empty dishes
lines: A feeding tray holds two empty dishes: USUAL FOOD and SPECIAL TREAT.
detail: A note says ACCEPTED BOTH. THEREFORE HAPPY TO REMAIN.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-2.title: The uncoated bowl
lines: Five bowls shine with new glaze. A sixth has a worn patch on its rim.
detail: Only the worn bowl has been pulled close to a sleeping mat.

NR-kitchens-cellars-clue-3.title: One more improvement
lines: A recipe begins with a simple bowl of soup. Additions run down the page and onto the table.
detail: At the bottom, somebody drew a spoon. It has a question mark beside it.

NR-greenhouse-clue-1.title: Soft moss, new latch
lines: Clean moss fills a little shelter. A bright new latch sits outside it.
detail: The moss is worn into a resting hollow. Small scrape marks reach toward the latch.

NR-greenhouse-clue-2.title: The turning pot
lines: A pot has turned so often that it has worn a circle into the shelf.
detail: Its leaves reach toward a small ordinary window, away from the brightest growing lamp.

NR-greenhouse-clue-3.title: Two pictures of a leaf
lines: A leaf in an old picture is small. The same notched leaf in a newer picture glows.
detail: Both leaves turn toward the same window. The notch appears in the same place.

NR-kennels-clue-1.title: Home confirmed
lines: A collar tray has a card: KNOWN HOME. AWAITING RETURN.
detail: A newer slip covers the return box: NOT YET SAFE. The collar’s name is too worn to read.

NR-kennels-clue-2.title: Treatment complete
lines: A care card reads ARRIVED LIMPING. WALKING COMFORTABLY. TREATMENT COMPLETE.
detail: The leaving box is still blank. A fresh blanket waits beside the card.

NR-kennels-clue-3.title: The favourite box
lines: Three splendid toys sit untouched. Their box has a well-worn sleeping hollow.
detail: A little resident settles into the box. One cardboard flap folds neatly over its nose.

NR-heart-clue-1.title: The old gate
lines: Newer bricks cover an old gate. Two words remain visible: GOING HOME.
detail: The gate has a handle on each side. The bricks were added after the handles.

NR-heart-clue-2.title: A name that stayed
lines: A clean name tile remains beneath the words WENT HOME.
detail: It is polished as carefully as the names marked STILL HERE.

NR-heart-clue-3.title: Two photographs
lines: Two pictures share a name. The later animal glows; the earlier one does not.
detail: Both tilt their heads beside the same crooked bowl. The glow has not replaced every familiar habit.

AFTER-foyer.label: Steady the edge of the dish.
AFTER-foyer.recap: You steadied the dish. The Butler served water to an animal behind the hatch.

AFTER-attic-observatory.label: Point to the empty telescope stand.
AFTER-attic-observatory.recap: You showed the empty stand. The Watcher secured the telescope and cleared the warning threads from the route.

AFTER-kitchens-cellars.label: Put the plain spoon beside the bowl.
AFTER-kitchens-cellars.recap: You put the spoon by the soup. The Confectioner used it and decided to keep it plain.

AFTER-greenhouse.label: Look at the fancy lamp.
AFTER-greenhouse.recap: You examined the lamp. The seedling kept turning away as it tilted closer. The Conservatory moved it and the vines aside; the seedling chose the window.

AFTER-kennels.label: Ask, “What if it comes back?”
AFTER-kennels.recap: You asked what would happen if the animal came back. The Kennelmaster prepared its bed and fresh water, then cleared the threshold so it could leave. Returning is an offer, not a requirement.

AFTER-heart.label: Tell the Keeper, “We can wait here.”
AFTER-heart.recap: You offered to wait. The Keeper opened the passage and left everyone room to decide what comes next.

END-GATE.label: Leave room for the animals.
END-GATE.recap: You left room. One animal stayed; another left and opened the gate from outside to return. The Keeper will wait for visitors.

Bean
TRICOLOUR GUINEA PIG, BROWN EYE PATCH

Wandered off during a family party. A cousin saw a tiny man in a red coat.

"Bean would accept lettuce from a burglar. That is not the same as agreeing to live somewhere."

Samir Haddad

Deadpan, exact about words, will negotiate with anything that talks back. Wants everybody comfortable, and is finding out that is not always the answer.

PERSISTENT PERK
Ask What It Means

Every Curiosity adds one option that asks what accepting actually costs, and the house has to answer before you choose.
